title: Host Health / Cluster Overview — Node & k3s Control Plane
description: Node-level health for MinecraftMachine (single-node k3s). Metrics come from the NATIVE node_exporter binary at 192.168.40.208:9100 — there is deliberately no node-exporter DaemonSet, so 'node' here means the real bare-metal host, not a container view of it.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Whole-host CPU, all 16 threads averaged. Includes the desktop session and any non-k8s process — not just pods.

panels.title: Memory Used
panels.description: 1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal. MemAvailable already discounts reclaimable page cache, so this is the number that matters for eviction risk.

panels.title: Root Disk Used (/ — 5900rpm HDD)
panels.description: / lives on /dev/sda2 (ST4000DM000, 5900rpm). k3s image store, all local-path PVCs and the Minecraft world all share this spindle.

panels.title: Node Ready
panels.description: kube-state-metrics view of the k3s Node object. If this flips to NotReady while the node_exporter panels still update, the problem is k3s/kubelet, not the host.

panels.title: Load Average vs Core Count
panels.description: The flat 'cores' line is the saturation reference: load1 above it means processes are queueing for CPU (or blocked on I/O — on this box, usually the HDD).

panels.title: CPU by Mode (% of total capacity)
panels.description: iowait rising while user/system stay flat is the signature of HDD contention rather than a real CPU shortage.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$node", mode!="idle"}[5m])) / on() group_left() count(count by (cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$node"})) * 100

panels.title: Memory — 15 GiB total, and that is the binding constraint on this host
Memory Breakdown vs Total Capacity
panels.description: The dashed red line is physical RAM (~15 GiB) — the hard ceiling. The dashed orange line is the kubelet's system-reserved=3Gi: memory below it is fenced off from the scheduler for the desktop session and system. Pods CANNOT swap (kubelet sets memory.swap.max=0 on cgroup v2), so a container at its limit is OOM-killed outright — the swap panels below are about host/desktop pressure only.

panels.title: Scheduled Pod Memory Requests vs Allocatable
panels.description: What the k3s scheduler thinks it has committed. Allocatable is already reduced by system-reserved=3Gi. If requests approach allocatable, new pods go Pending — that is a scheduling failure, distinct from the host actually running out of RAM.

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory"} * on(namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running"} == 1))
sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="memory"} * on(namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running"} == 1))

panels.title: Swap Activity (host thrashing indicator)
panels.description: Sustained non-zero swap-in/out means the HOST (desktop session, system processes) is paging. Containers are excluded from swap entirely, so this never explains a pod OOMKill — but it does explain a laggy desktop and extra HDD contention.

panels.title: Available Memory (eviction floor 500 MiB)
panels.description: kubelet was installed with eviction-hard=memory.available<500Mi. When this stat enters the red band, the kubelet starts evicting pods by QoS class.

panels.title: Disk — / is a 5900rpm HDD (ST4000DM000); I/O contention is a known, real concern
Disk I/O Latency (avg service time per op)
panels.description: read_time/reads_completed and write_time/writes_completed. On a 5900rpm spindle, healthy is roughly <20 ms; sustained >100 ms means the queue is deep and everything touching disk (Minecraft chunk saves, Prometheus compaction, Loki chunk flush) is waiting. Gaps are normal — the ratio is undefined when there were no operations in the interval.

panels.title: Disk Utilisation (% of time busy)
panels.description: node_disk_io_time_seconds_total rate. 100% means the device never had an idle moment in the interval — the drive is saturated and latency above will be climbing.

panels.title: Avg Queue Depth (weighted I/O time)
panels.description: rate(node_disk_io_time_weighted_seconds_total). Values well above 1 mean requests are stacking up behind the spindle. This is the single best 'the HDD is the bottleneck' signal on this box.

panels.title: Filesystem Inode Usage
panels.description: A filesystem can fail to create new files while still showing free space. k3s image layers, local-path PVCs and Loki chunks all create large numbers of small files.

panels.title: Host Network I/O (physical interfaces)
panels.description: Excludes loopback, the flannel/cni overlay and every pod veth — that traffic is on the panel to the right.

panels.title: Cluster Overlay Network (cni0 / flannel.1)
panels.description: Pod-to-pod and pod-to-service traffic. If this is flat at zero while pods are clearly talking, suspect the ufw FORWARD policy (DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=DROP) blackholing 10.42.0.0/16.

panels.title: kube-system Pods Not Ready
panels.description: NOTE: on k3s, the apiserver, scheduler and controller-manager run inside the single k3s process — they are NOT pods, so there are no kube_pod_* series for them. What this counts is the add-on control plane that IS podded: coredns, local-path-provisioner, metrics-server. If k3s itself is down, this panel goes stale rather than red — use 'Node Ready' at the top of the dashboard for that.

panels.title: Prometheus Scrape Targets Down
panels.description: count(up == 0). Catches the failure mode where a dashboard looks 'fine' only because its exporter stopped being scraped — e.g. the native node_exporter on :9100 or minecraft_exporter on :9202.

panels.title: Node Pressure Conditions Active
panels.description: MemoryPressure / DiskPressure / PIDPressure. Any of these true means the kubelet is already taking defensive action (refusing to schedule, evicting, or garbage-collecting images).

panels.title: kube-system Pods
panels.description: Phase and restart count for the podded part of the k3s control plane.

panels.title: kube-system Container Restarts (rolling 1h)
panels.description: Anything other than a flat zero here means a control-plane add-on is crash-looping. CoreDNS restarting right after install is the classic ufw-FORWARD-DROP symptom.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: k10temp = Ryzen CPU, nvme = the NVMe (currently holding a dd'd live installer, not in use by k3s), acpitz = chassis. From node_exporter's hwmon collector.
